title: Show a history/trend view of past daily self-test entries -- GET /api/daily-homework (list) has zero frontend consumer
description: Filed by the frontend-backend-feature-gap-audit task. `GET /api/daily-homework` (`operation_id: list_daily_homework`, `backend/app/api/routers/homework.py`) returns `DailyHomeworkListResponse` -- 'Every recorded self-test entry, most recent date first', the router's own docstring calling it 'a history/trend view of how "ready to trade" scores have looked over time' -- but grep confirms `frontend/src/api/homework.ts` has no caller for it at all (only `GET /today`, `POST /api/daily-homework`, and `GET /yesterday-trading-suggestion` are wired up), and `frontend/src/features/homework/` has no history/list component or hook of any kind. `DailyHomeworkPage` (`frontend-daily-homework-page`) only ever shows today's single entry via `DailyHomeworkForm`/`HomeworkScoreBanner` (today's recorded scores, or today's suggested defaults if not yet recorded) -- a user can dutifully record a self-test every single day but can never see how their own readiness score has trended over the past weeks or months, despite the backend already fully supporting exactly that view with no further backend work needed. Neither `frontend-daily-homework-page` nor either of its two followup tasks mentions deferring a history view as a conscious decision -- this was simply never built.

checklist.step: Add a `listDailyHomework()`/`getDailyHomeworkHistory()` function to frontend/src/api/homework.ts (GET /api/daily-homework) plus a TanStack Query hook and MSW mock.
Decide presentation: a plain table (date, the 5 component scores, total_score, band) vs. a trend chart of total_score/band over time, or both -- record the decision and rationale.

Add the history view to DailyHomeworkPage (a new section, or its own sub-route reached from there) -- reuse HomeworkScoreBanner's existing red/yellow/green band-coloring convention rather than inventing a new color scheme.
Tests + a Storybook story for the new component(s); confirm the 90% coverage gate still holds.

decisions.decision: Presentation: a plain table only (date, the 5 component scores, total_score, a band chip), via the existing common/DataTable, with no lightweight-charts trend chart -- no dataviz-skill chart work needed for this task.
decisions.rationale: This self-test is answered at most once per calendar day, so the series is inherently low-cardinality -- nothing like the hundreds-of-bars OHLC/indicator history features/stocks/components/ plots with Lightweight Charts (utils/chart.ts's createBaseChart etc.), which exists specifically for that denser, zoomable, multi-pane use case. A single total_score trend line would also discard the per-question breakdown (which of the 5 answers actually drove a particularly low/high day), which is exactly the kind of diagnostic detail Elder's self-test is meant to surface -- a table row showing all 5 components plus the total reads as more useful at a glance than a sparkline would, for the data density this feature actually has. Rejected: (a) a lightweight-charts trend line of total_score, which would have required loading the dataviz skill and pulling in the same charting machinery used for price/indicator panes, for a feature whose data is sparse by construction (one point per day the user manually visits) and whose most valuable information (the per-question breakdown) a single scalar line can't show anyway; (b) both table and chart together, rejected for the same reason -- the chart would have added UI surface and maintenance cost without adding information the table doesn't already convey more completely.

decisions.decision: New DailyHomeworkHistoryTable component lives under features/homework/components/ (not components/common/), added as a new section on the existing DailyHomeworkPage (not a separate sub-route), and the red/yellow/green band-coloring convention is shared by extracting HomeworkScoreBanner's SEVERITY_BY_BAND map and isTooPerfectBand predicate into a new plain (non-component) features/homework/components/band.ts module that both HomeworkScoreBanner.tsx and DailyHomeworkHistoryTable.tsx import, rather than inventing a second mapping or exporting those two consts directly from HomeworkScoreBanner.tsx.
decisions.rationale: Placement: every column DailyHomeworkHistoryTable renders (physical_state_score, band, etc.) is a homework self-test domain concept -- Frontend.md §3's placement test puts this under features/homework/components/, matching HomeworkScoreBanner's own placement rationale, not components/common/ (which would need a domain-agnostic, generic-props component instead). Page layout: a same-page section (below DailyHomeworkForm) rather than a dedicated /homework/history sub-route -- the history view is a small, read-only complement to the one daily action this page exists for, not a separate workflow a user navigates to deliberately; keeping it on one page also means NavDrawer needs no new entry and a user sees their trend immediately after recording today's entry, with no extra navigation. Shared band convention: an initial attempt exported SEVERITY_BY_BAND/isTooPerfectBand directly from HomeworkScoreBanner.tsx, but that tripped the repo's (previously zero-warning) eslint react-refresh/only-export-components rule the moment a second component (DailyHomeworkHistoryTable) imported them, since that rule flags any .tsx file whose exports aren't all components. Moving both into a new plain band.ts file (mirroring the existing metricHelpContent.ts precedent elsewhere in features/*/components/ for a domain-specific, non-component helper shared by more than one component in a folder) keeps eslint clean while still giving both components the exact same mapping/predicate, satisfying the checklist's 'reuse HomeworkScoreBanner's existing ... convention rather than inventing a new color scheme' requirement precisely.

decisions.decision: useRecordDailyHomework's onSuccess now also invalidates homeworkKeys.history (not just homeworkKeys.today).
decisions.rationale: Not originally in the checklist, but add-frontend-feature's own step 3 treats an omitted invalidation as a stale-UI bug, not a style nit: a successful POST /api/daily-homework always changes GET /api/daily-homework's list too (either adding today's row or overwriting its existing one), so leaving the history query un-invalidated would have shown a stale history table immediately after a successful submission until some unrelated refetch happened to occur. Confirmed end to end via a live browser walkthrough (submitting today's entry updates the History table's row immediately, no manual reload) -- see this task's report.
